creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Statistics
AP Statistics
Confounding Variable
Identifying Confounding
Lurking Variable
Correlation vs Causation
description: Interactive causal diagram and simulated scatterplot showing how a confounding variable creates an apparent relationship between X and Y, and what remains when the confounder is held constant.

learningObjectives: Analyze how a variable associated with both X and Y creates an alternative explanation for an observed association (Analyze)
Compare the observed relationship with the relationship that remains after the confounder is held constant (Analyze)
Explain why a confounder must be associated with both the explanatory and the response variable (Understand)
prerequisites: Scatterplots, correlation, and least-squares slope (Chapters 6 and 7)

keyQuestions: Is the third variable related to both X and Y?
How much of the relationship remains when the confounder is held constant?
commonMisconceptions: Any lurking variable is automatically a confounder, even if it is unrelated to X
Finding a confounder means X has no effect on Y at all
assessmentOpportunities: Student states both requirements for a confounder and demonstrates each with the sliders
Student correctly predicts the direction of change in slope before clicking Hold C Constant
Student explains the difference between the observed slope and the direct effect in context
